verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced independently. (a) Direct diff vs h5 target test0: exp-propagator scheme with n=9999 steps matches target u to maxabs 7.79e-12; n=10000 misses by 6.84e-04 -> np.allclose False. (b) Official scoring: steptest 55.4 with n_steps=int(round(T/dt)) (=10000; same solve_SH that PASSES 55.1) -> 'RESULT step 55.4: FAIL' (AssertionError on test 0). (c) 55.1 targets verified to encode exactly (5,5,10) steps (test1 bit-exact at n=5, off by 1.1e-2 at n=4/6; test2 1.6e-15 at n=10, 1.6e-2 at n=9/11). HOWEVER, one first-pass sub-claim is REFUTED: 'no single step-counting rule yields (5, 10, 9999)' is false. The float-accumulating no-overshoot loop `t=0; while t+dt<=T: step; t+=dt` (also `while t<=T-dt`) yields exactly (5, 5, 10, 9999) for all four (T,dt) combos, and an implementation using it PASSES BOTH 55.1 and 55.4 under official steptest (verified: 55.4 PASS in 39s, 55.1 PASS). So a survivable path exists and the problem is not strictly internally inconsistent; severity recalibrated blocker -> major. It remains a genuine D7: the spec says 'stop at a final time T' and T/dt==10000.0 exactly in IEEE double, so the mathematically correct step count is 10000; the targets encode the reference's float-fragile loop stopping at t=49.995. Every common counting rule (int(T/dt), round(T/dt), ceil, len(np.arange(0,T,dt)), and `while t<T` which gives 11 steps on 55.1 test2) fails either 55.1 or 55.4, so in practice most competent solvers fail 55.4.

verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced. Bin-center identities verified bit-exact: 55.3 test0 target 0.9774342463948407 == 5.5*sqrt(2)*pi/25 (N=50, nbins=N//2=25 over [0, max|k|=sqrt(2)pi]); test1 target 2.221441469079183 == 7.5*sqrt(2)*pi/15 (N=30). Official steptest 55.3: nbins=N//2 + 0.5*q0 proximity -> PASS; nbins=N -> FAIL; nbins=100 -> FAIL; threshold 0.1*q0 -> FAIL (test1 peak dev = 0.2214 = 11.07% of q0=2); threshold = one bin width -> PASSES 55.3 but FAILS 55.4 (verified from frozen 55.4 targets: test4 N=200 q0=1 peak at 0.955220, dev 0.044780 vs bin width 0.044429, ratio 1.0079 -> rejected -> (False,0) vs target (True, 0.95522)). One refinement to the first-pass framing: the feasible threshold window is ONE-SIDED, not narrow — no test ever requires REJECTING a peak (all False-target cases have no peaks at all above min_height: 55.3 test2 k=0 boundary spike invisible to find_peaks; 55.4 test2 Sk_max 7e-20 < 1e-12), so any threshold >= 0.111*q0, including omitting the proximity check entirely, passes everything. The defect stands: neither nbins=N//2, nor the bin range, nor a threshold loose enough (>11% of q0) is stated ('within some reasonable tolerance threshold'), and natural tight choices (10% of q0, one bin width) fail; the docstring's 'narrowness' criterion is never exercised by any test.

verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced. Official steptest 55.1: exact exponential k-space propagator exp(dt*(2k^2/q0^2 - k^4/q0^4)) + explicit-Euler local substep -> PASS (test2 matches target to maxrel 2.3e-14); semi-implicit factor 1/(1-dt*L) -> FAIL (maxrel 4.7e-2 on test2); explicit k-space Euler (1+dt*L) -> FAIL (maxrel 5.4e-2). Test1 uniform-field value 0.9390147345933418 bit-matches explicit-Euler local updates. Background only says 'we tranform the tranport term ... to k-space, and update it in k-space based on u1' — no integration rule for either substep. The attack 'split-step canonically means exact exponential of the linear part' does not rescue it: a split-step purist would also integrate the local Bernoulli ODE du/dt=(eps-1)u-u^3 exactly over dt, which differs from the encoded explicit-Euler local substep at O(dt^2) and fails allclose; the target encodes a specific MIXED scheme (Euler local + exact exponential k-space) that no principled reading uniquely selects.

fix.after: 2. Next, we transform the transport term $-[2q_0^{-2}\nabla^2 + q_0^{-4}\nabla^4]u$ to k-space and integrate it EXACTLY over one time step: multiply each Fourier mode of $u_1$ by $\exp[dt\,(2k^2/q_0^2 - k^4/q_0^4)]$ (grid spacing $dx=1$, $k$ from 2*pi*np.fft.fftfreq(N,1)), then invert back to real space with the IFFT to obtain $u_{N+1}$. For step 1, use a single explicit-Euler update: $u_1 = u_N + dt\,(\epsilon u_N - u_N - u_N^3)$.

verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced (normalization). Raw Sk = fftshift(|fft2(u)|^2) matches the test0 target to maxabs 2.8e-13 (target max 33366.6). summary: All 7 first-pass findings are confirmed by independent reproduction (official steptest + bit-level target forensics), with one material correction: the 55.4 off-by-one (targets at 9999 steps, t=49.995 instead of T=50) is real and fails every common step-count rule, but it is NOT internally inconsistent — a float-accumulating no-overshoot loop (while t+dt<=T) yields (5,10,9999) and passes both 55.1 and 55.4 officially, so severity is recalibrated blocker->major (practically near-blocker). The problem is fully fixable to fair with modest effort: regenerate the six 55.4 u/Sk targets at exactly 10000 steps (booleans/modes verified unchanged, recipe provided) and pin four conventions via prompt/doc edits (exact-exponential k-space + Euler local scheme; raw |fft2|^2; meshgrid indexing='ij'; N//2-bin radial histogram with a >=0.5*q0-style proximity threshold). Two additional minor issues found (cosmetic return_line naming; the proximity-rejection branch is never tested).
